blocks.content: If you have not applied the fix on your database yet, skip this step. When you have, complete the following steps:

Open **Queries overview**.

Find the same query you recorded before the fix.

Compare the query with what you recorded.

- **Duration (avg)** should decrease.
- **Errors** should not increase.
- **Calls** should remain stable.

For example, watch the same three numbers over time to see whether the improvement holds under varying load.

Record whether the index is being used.

If the fix was an index, the new index should be on the table. The highlighted operation should read through an index rather than scan the whole table, and the row estimates should have decreased.

If the plan has not changed after an index was added, table statistics may be outdated. Outdated table statistics can make the estimates inaccurate. PostgreSQL uses **ANALYZE** and MySQL uses **ANALYZE TABLE** to update table statistics. Check the plan again afterward. Those commands are on [Improve slow queries](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/monitor-applications/database-observability/optimize/improve-slow-queries/).

blocks.content: Record whether every run got faster, or only some of them, and whether any run got slower.

You have compared duration, errors, and calls with what you recorded. You have also checked whether the plan uses an index where the fix was an index, and whether every run got faster or only some of them.
